routines.summary: 24 site checks, 18 browser checks with deliberate breaks, 91 unit tests and the LinkML check run before every publish. A check is trusted only once its deliberate break is caught.
12 requirements met, 12 partly; 2 of 4 release gates met; 19 of 19 repository files in place.
Review date, organisation list, change-flag baseline and watched sources, each against its own limit.
32 defects found and fixed, each with a check that stops it coming back. Automation reports and rebuilds; only a person changes content, settings or the open register (20 items).

checks.what: every page sets a Content Security Policy with no unsafe sources.
no script, stylesheet, image or font loaded from another host (E2: self-contained pages).
no email address anywhere in the published files (COL-02), metadata and data included.
ids are unique on every page.
every internal link resolves, to a file and, if it has one, an anchor on that page.
every table is captioned, has scoped headers and sits in a labelled, focusable scroll region.
every page describes itself: artefact id, version, class, as-of, review date, and JSON-LD.
every page carries the colophon: disclaimers, licence, version, QR code, barcode and the contact form.
the first focusable element on every page is the skip link to main.
no deck or film files in the repository or the site, unless the owner says so for that piece.
no inline executable scripts and no inline event handlers, so the Content Security Policy can forbid them.
every page shows the status banner: proposed, not endorsed, not an official service.
every page has lang="en-GB" and a unique title.
no page over 1,500 KB with what it loads from this site (envelope: median page 1,500 KB).
every meaningful image has an accessible name; decorative icons are hidden.
no unrendered template placeholders, such as [layers] or [prov("K")], in page text (D-007).
llms.txt and llms-full.txt exist, every page is listed in llms.txt, and every link in it resolves to a built file.
no style attributes in any page: the CSP (style-src 'self') blocks them, so they silently do nothing (D-018).
every guided tour stop points at something on its page, so no tour silently skips a step.
every page offers "Suggest a change to this page", pointing at an issue form that exists and naming that page.
no protective markings or handling caveats anywhere public: pages, downloads and the requirements file (ADR 0015, RQ-18).
no old directorate name and no personal or team details anywhere: pages, downloads or repository files. Contact is by form only.

change flags agree with downloads/changes-since.json: each new or updated page says so under its title and in the global bar, and each changed section's heading is flagged (the Data Quality Commons pattern).
no email address in the repository's own files either; test fixtures may use reserved example domains only.

gates.gate: Reuse assessed for every new term
gates.evidence: Each property records whether it is reused, changed or new against the xGov MEM and DCAT; not yet a blocking check.

gates.gate: Every rule traced to a test
gates.evidence: tests/test_profile.py fails the build if a rule has no deliberate break.

gates.gate: No open serious semantic-loss or disclosure defect
gates.evidence: The defect register is complete and C-22 blocks protective markings; semantic-loss defects are not yet graded by severity.
Conformance levels come from the kit; no allied or controlled compatibility is claimed (RQ-15, RQ-29).

oversight.digest: Every Monday the digest routine opens one issue (label digest) listing what every routine did, what failed and what needs a person. It closes last week's.
oversight.undo: Every tier 1 change is one commit by github-actions, with the routine named in its message; revert it to undo.
oversight.audit: Workflow run logs are kept by GitHub for 90 days; the digest links to the runs.

routines.when: every push, every pull request, Mondays 06:23 UTC, on request
routines.does: Builds the site, runs every check and deliberate break, runs the health run for the Status page, and publishes main.
routines.changes: The published site only (gh-pages), after every check passes.

routines.does: Opens or updates an issue labelled health when a source changed or is unreachable, the review date is near or a page is too heavy; closes it when healthy.

routines.when: a person pushes a version tag, or presses Run on the Release workflow
routines.does: Builds and checks the tagged version and publishes a GitHub release with the profile files and the site.
routines.changes: A GitHub release. Only a person starts it.

routines.does: Records the section baseline from the released tag, so change flags show what changed since that release; checks the site, commits content/section-baseline.json and republishes.
Refreshes the organisation list from GOV.UK, repairs a change-flag baseline that lags the latest release, and reminds about the review date.
routines.changes: profile/organisations.json and content/section-baseline.json, after every check passes. A large organisation change (more than 25 rows) becomes a pull request instead. Review reminders are issues.

routines.does: Labels contact, defect, change request and conformance claim issues that have waited too long for a reply (needs-reply) or a decision (overdue).
Writes the weekly operations digest for the owner: the Status page, what each routine did, failed runs, issues waiting, pull requests open and decisions needed.
routines.changes: One issue a week (label digest); closes the previous one.

routines.does: Keeps the repository labels in line with .github/labels.yml.

routines.when: every push, every pull request, Mondays
routines.does: Scans the code for security problems.

routines.when: Mondays, on request, when branch rules change
routines.does: OpenSSF Scorecard: an independent check of how the repository is run.
Stops a pull request that adds a dependency with a known moderate or worse vulnerability.

occurrences.label: occurrence
occurrences.how: Anyone, person or routine, reports a near miss or a surprise with the occurrence issue form. No blame: the report asks what happened and what would have stopped it, never who. A routine that stops itself (kill switch, failed gate, abort rule) says so in the digest.
occurrences.follow_up: Every occurrence closes with either a check that would have caught it (as for a defect) or a recorded reason why none is needed.

never: Change repository settings, rulesets, secrets or the kill switch.
Delete a branch, tag, release, issue or file a person made.
Send anything outside the repository (pull requests or issues elsewhere, email, posts).
Change the profile, its codelists, the requirements, the registers or any page content written by a person.
